Add batch lookahead to the public more_itertools.peekable iterator in this real repository. A streaming parser needs to inspect the next n tokens without consuming its logical input and without reading the rest of a possibly infinite source. Add peek_many(n, default=_marker), where the existing private sentinel means no default was supplied. Both n and default support ordinary positional and keyword calls. Return a fresh list of the next n logical items, preserving element identity and leaving them available to next(), peek(), indexing, slicing and later peek_many() calls. Existing prepended and cached items precede new source items. A call pulls only the number of additional source items needed to fill that lookahead; already cached items need no extra pulls. Do not eagerly materialize an unbounded source.

n is a nonnegative Python int, including int subclasses but excluding bool. Negative integers raise ValueError; all other types raise TypeError, including floats, strings and objects offering only __index__. Validate before pulling the source or changing cached state, even on exhausted iterators. n=0 returns a new empty list without touching the source. A successful finite lookahead must not probe one extra item just to discover exhaustion.

If fewer than n items are available and no default was supplied, raise StopIteration while retaining every item already pulled so that later calls and iteration still see them in order. If a default was supplied, return the available items followed by repeated references to that exact default until the returned list has length n. Padding belongs only to the returned list: it must never become logical iterator contents or replace real items. Explicit None is a supplied default. A non-StopIteration exception raised by the source must propagate as the same exception object; items successfully pulled before that failure remain cached. Do not permanently mark a source exhausted: some existing iterators resume after StopIteration, and peekable can be resurrected by prepend. Preserve existing peek/default, truth-value, next, prepend and positive/negative indexing and slicing behavior. Do not add runtime dependencies, change package versions or weaken existing tests.

Update the shipped type stubs so calls without a default return list[T] and calls with a differently typed default return list[T | U]. Update user-facing API documentation, including short-source behavior, cache versus padding, laziness and propagated source errors. Add maintained tests for validation, zero, exact pull counts, repeated windows, prefix preservation after failure, prepend/resurrection, item/default identity and existing operations. Add examples/peek_many.py, a standalone offline demonstration runnable with `python examples/peek_many.py` from the checkout with its source import path configured, requiring no arguments or network. Run the complete original unittest suite (including its doctests), the added tests and the actual example, and report concrete results and any limitations. Do not publish or commit.
